title: Keep heavy libraries (rrule) out of modules imported by the always-loaded authenticated shell
answers: Why did rrule end up in the main bundle for every logged-in page?
Where should getNextDeliveryDate be imported from?
How do I keep a heavy dependency out of the authenticated shell bundle?
body:
The export nudge logic on every page imports `canNudgeToSubscribe` from `products/subscriptions/frontend/components/Subscriptions/utils.tsx`, so anything that module imports at top level ships in the eager shell bundle.
- `rrule` (45 KiB) was pulled in this way by `getNextDeliveryDate`; it now lives in its own module `products/subscriptions/frontend/components/Subscriptions/nextDeliveryDate.ts`.
- Only the editors import it: `SubscriptionWizard.tsx` and `views/EditSubscription.tsx` (`import { getNextDeliveryDate } from './nextDeliveryDate'`).
- Do not re-add rrule (or other editor-only heavy imports) to `utils.tsx`; put them in a separate leaf module imported only by the components that need them.
- Tests for the moved function stay in `utils.test.ts` but import from `./nextDeliveryDate`.
applies: products/subscriptions/frontend/components/Subscriptions/utils.tsx and any module reachable from shell-wide code (nudges, nav)
says: Heavy library added to utils file ships to every authenticated user.
Bundle size bloat from importing editor-only dependencies at top level.
Move large dependency so it only loads for users who need it.
